deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a heavily corrected draft of the methodological preface to Riemann's posthumous fragment on the mechanics of the ear. The fragment was published by Henle in 1867 in the Zeitschrift für rationelle Medicin as 'Mechanik des Ohres', and it appears in the Gesammelte Werke. The heading reads 'Ueber die in der Physiologie der feineren Sinnesorgane anzuwendende Methode'. The argument runs as follows.

(1) Two foundations. Besides the general laws of nature, the physiology of a sense organ needs two special foundations. One is psychophysical: the empirical determination of what the organ achieves (its 'Leistungen'). The other is anatomical: the study of its structure.

(2) Two routes. Accordingly there are two ways to learn the organ's functions. (a) Start from the structure and derive the laws of interaction of its parts and the effect of external stimuli. (b) Start from the achievements of the organ and try to explain them.

(3) Critique of route (a). This is the anatomist's natural route: for each component he asks what influence it has on the whole. It works for the motor organs. For the finer sense organs it fails, because the physical properties of microscopic parts can be determined only uncertainly and very imprecisely. Investigators therefore supplement them with guesses about the purpose of each part, made by analogy or teleology. Since that purpose can only be guessed on this route, it cannot lead to secure results.

(4) A long struck-through passage describes route (b). Here the achievements may be regarded as the 'purpose' of the organ, but this purpose is given by observation and experiment rather than conjectured. In the actual investigation the notion of purpose can be dropped entirely: cause and effect suffice once the organ's construction is set aside.

(5) Analytic and synthetic are relative terms. Every synthesis rests on the result of a preceding analysis; here the general laws of motion are the presupposed result of earlier analysis. Every analysis needs confirmation or correction by a subsequent synthesis.

(6) The page breaks off: 'The first, predominantly synthetic procedure is for the theory +'.

Context from the previous page: the 'sound curve' is introduced as the logarithm of the rate of pressure change. Its shape is then invariant under scaling of amplitude, because log(c f) = log c + log f, a vertical shift. Faithful transmission by the middle ear therefore means a constant amplification ratio between air and labyrinth fluid. No computation appears on this page itself.

results.what: Methodological distinction for sensory physiology. The synthetic route goes from anatomy and physical properties of parts to function. The analytic route goes from measured performance of the organ to the mechanism. Riemann criticises teleological guessing on the first route and stresses that analysis and synthesis depend on each other.
results.modern_name: Inverse-problem / system-identification (black-box) approach versus forward modelling, in philosophy of physiological method
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's own published fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' (posthumous, Henle 1867); related ideas in Helmholtz, Fechner (psychophysics)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the known, published methodological introduction to Riemann's 'Mechanik des Ohres' (Gesammelte Werke). It contains no mathematics and no unpublished result.

checkable.asserts: From the previous page's context: the log-scaled 'Klangcurve' changes only by an additive constant under amplitude scaling. Its shape is therefore independent of sound intensity.

transcription_corrections: The top-left marginal heading is uncertain. It may read 'Mechanik des Ohr.' or 'Inhalt des Ohr.' rather than 'Princip der Phys.'
Line 2: the image appears to read '...bedarf ... zwei besondere Grundlagen nöthig'. The verb is corrected in place (possibly 'sind ... nöthig'), so 'bedarf [-ist-]' is a conflation.
'Der erste Weg liegt dem Anatomen am nächsten' is consistent with the image. 'inductorische Weg' near the end of the first paragraph may instead be a corrected word ('synthetische'?); uncertain.

The marginal insertion near the end of the first paragraph is better read as 'daher die Ergänzung durch Analogie oder Teleologie'. This matches the published text's contrast with teleological conjecture.
The 'durch Rückschauung' insertion is doubtful. The image suggests 'durch Kunstverfahren' or similar; mark it as illegible rather than guessed.
